```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Purpose

Reads the raw Alchemer export, checks that every column lines up with the variable dictionary, renames the columns to the simplified names, and saves the renamed dataset under a new filename. Use the renamed file for all work from here on.

**Inputs**

- `data/raw/` Alchemer export (fill in `raw_file` below)
- `variable-dictionary-Q4_3.R` in `scripts/functions/` or `scripts/` (the dictionary, one row per export column)

**Outputs**

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `data/processed/00_Q4_3_renamed.rds` | All 115 columns, renamed, column types guessed (use this one in R) |
| `data/processed/00_Q4_3_renamed.csv` | Same data as a CSV (UTF-8 with BOM so Excel reads special characters) |
| `docs/Q4_3_variable-dictionary.xlsx` | Sheets: dictionary, flagged, blocks |
| `output/00_Q4_3_pulse_rename-variables/` | Column check and PANAS duplicate check |

## Packages and paths

```{r packages}
# Install any missing packages, then load
pkgs <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "readr", "readxl", "openxlsx")
to_install <- pkgs[!vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
invisible(lapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE))
```

```{r paths}
# ---- Project folder: every path below is built from here ----
project_root <- "C:/path/to/Q4_3_Pulse"
proj <- function(...) file.path(project_root, ...)

if (!dir.exists(project_root)) stop("Project folder not found: ", project_root)

script_name <- "00_Q4_3_pulse_rename-variables"
out_dir <- proj("output", script_name)
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(proj("data", "processed"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(proj("docs"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Use the first copy of a file found in scripts/functions/ or scripts/
find_script <- function(filename) {
  candidates <- c(proj("scripts", "functions", filename), proj("scripts", filename))
  hit <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  hit[1]
}

# Shared theme and helpers, if present
setup_file <- find_script("project-setup.R")
if (!is.na(setup_file)) source(setup_file)

# Variable dictionary
dict_file <- find_script("variable-dictionary-Q4_3.R")
if (is.na(dict_file)) {
  stop("variable-dictionary-Q4_3.R not found in scripts/functions/ or scripts/ under ", project_root)
}
source(dict_file)

# ---- Fill in before knitting ----
raw_file <- proj("data", "raw", "FILL_IN_alchemer_export.csv")   # .csv or .xlsx
if (!file.exists(raw_file)) stop("Raw export not found: ", raw_file)
```

## Read the raw export

Everything is read as text first so nothing gets coerced before the check. `name_repair = "minimal"` keeps the export headers exactly as they are, including the duplicated PANAS headers.

```{r read}
read_export <- function(path) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(path))
  if (ext %in% c("xlsx", "xls")) {
    readxl::read_excel(path, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "minimal")
  } else {
    readr::read_csv(
      path,
      col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
      name_repair = "minimal",
      locale = readr::locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
      na = c("", "NA")
    )
  }
}

raw <- read_export(raw_file)
dim(raw)
```

## Check the export against the dictionary

Export headers are full question text, so each column is matched on position plus `header_key`: the first 40 characters of the header, lowercase letters and numbers only. Knitting stops if anything has moved.

```{r check}
make_header_key <- function(x, n = 40) {
  substr(gsub("[^a-z0-9]", "", tolower(x)), 1, n)
}

if (ncol(raw) != nrow(var_dict_q4_3)) {
  stop("Export has ", ncol(raw), " columns; dictionary has ", nrow(var_dict_q4_3), ".")
}

column_check <- var_dict_q4_3 |>
  select(col, new_name, header_key) |>
  mutate(
    export_header = names(raw),
    export_key    = make_header_key(names(raw)),
    match         = export_key == header_key
  )

readr::write_csv(column_check, file.path(out_dir, "column-check.csv"))

if (!all(column_check$match)) {
  print(filter(column_check, !match) |> select(col, new_name, header_key, export_key))
  stop(sum(!column_check$match), " column(s) do not match the dictionary. See column-check.csv.")
}

message("All ", nrow(column_check), " columns match.")
```

## Rename

```{r rename}
renamed <- raw
names(renamed) <- var_dict_q4_3$new_name

# Guess column types now that names are set (numbers become numeric, text stays text)
renamed <- readr::type_convert(renamed, col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_guess()))

glimpse(renamed, width = 100)
```

### PANAS duplicate check

The export carries PANAS items 1 to 5 twice in both D1 (`panas_pre_`) and D3 (`panas_post_`). The first copy is named `*_dup`. The table below shows which copy holds responses, so the empty copy can be set to `drop` in the dictionary.

```{r panas-dups}
panas_items <- c("interested", "distressed", "excited", "upset", "strong")

panas_dup_check <- tidyr::expand_grid(wave = c("pre", "post"), item = panas_items) |>
  mutate(
    variable    = paste0("panas_", wave, "_", item),
    n_dup_copy  = vapply(paste0(variable, "_dup"), \(v) sum(!is.na(renamed[[v]])), integer(1)),
    n_main_copy = vapply(variable, \(v) sum(!is.na(renamed[[v]])), integer(1))
  ) |>
  select(variable, n_dup_copy, n_main_copy)

readr::write_csv(panas_dup_check, file.path(out_dir, "panas-duplicate-check.csv"))
knitr::kable(panas_dup_check)
```

## Save

```{r save}
saveRDS(renamed, proj("data", "processed", "00_Q4_3_renamed.rds"))
readr::write_excel_csv(renamed, proj("data", "processed", "00_Q4_3_renamed.csv"), na = "")

wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, "dictionary")
openxlsx::writeDataTable(wb, "dictionary", var_dict_q4_3)
openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, "flagged")
openxlsx::writeDataTable(wb, "flagged", filter(var_dict_q4_3, status != "keep"))
openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, "blocks")
openxlsx::writeDataTable(
  wb, "blocks",
  var_dict_q4_3 |> count(block, status) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
)
openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, proj("docs", "Q4_3_variable-dictionary.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)

message("Saved ", nrow(renamed), " rows x ", ncol(renamed), " columns.")
```

## Notes from the skeleton

- **PANAS has 25 columns instead of 20 in both D1 and D3.** Items 1 to 5 repeat. Worth fixing the grid in Alchemer if the survey is still live.
- **Some columns aren't in the v6 programming doc:** the reverse-sentence attention check (`attn_reverse_text`), `demo_state_longest`, and `demo_insurance` with its write-in.
- **The export puts B3 (consent to share) before B2 (chat history access).**
- **Status counts:** 87 keep, 11 review, 17 drop. Every column is saved in the renamed file. Use `status` in the dictionary to select columns downstream, for example `select(renamed, all_of(filter(var_dict_q4_3, status == "keep")$new_name))`.
